1.0.0::CM001.document: CM001: Fit matters more than brand or price.

1.0.0::CM002.document: CM002: The shoulder seam of any jacket or shirt must sit exactly at the shoulder bone.

1.0.0::CM003.document: CM003: Build every outfit around at least one neutral color.

1.0.0::CM004.document: CM004: Limit any outfit to a maximum of three colors.

1.0.0::CM005.document: CM005: Follow the 60-30-10 rule: 60% dominant, 30% secondary, 10% accent.

1.0.0::CM006.document: CM006: Never pair navy and black in the same outfit.

1.0.0::CM007.document: CM007: Never pair brown and black in the same outfit.

1.0.0::CM008.document: CM008: White is the most versatile shirt color in any wardrobe.

1.0.0::CM009.document: CM009: Navy is the most versatile trouser and jacket color in any wardrobe.

1.0.0::CM010.document: CM010: One bold pattern in an outfit is enough — everything else should be solid.

1.0.0::CM011.document: CM011: Stripes pair only with solids, never with other patterns.

1.0.0::CM012.document: CM012: Checks and plaids pair only with solids.

1.0.0::CM013.document: CM013: Denim acts as a neutral — it pairs with almost any color.

1.0.0::CM014.document: CM014: Never match denim jacket and denim jeans of the same wash.

1.0.0::CM015.document: CM015: Volume balance is essential — if the top is oversized, the bottom must be slim.

1.0.0::CM016.document: CM016: Never wear oversized top and oversized bottom simultaneously.

1.0.0::CM017.document: CM017: Dress for the occasion first, personal style second.

1.0.0::CM018.document: CM018: Overdressing is always preferable to underdressing in ambiguous situations.

1.0.0::CM019.document: CM019: A well-fitted inexpensive suit beats a poorly-fitted expensive one.

1.0.0::CM020.document: CM020: The collar point length should be proportional to tie width and lapel width.

1.0.0::CM021.document: CM021: Shirt cuff must show 0.5 inch below jacket sleeve in formal contexts.

1.0.0::CM022.document: CM022: Trouser break should be no break or half break for modern slim fits.

1.0.0::CM023.document: CM023: Trousers should sit at the natural waist without a belt to hold them up.

1.0.0::CM024.document: CM024: Shoes should be darker than or the same tone as trousers — never lighter.

1.0.0::CM025.document: CM025: Match belt color to shoe color in formal contexts.

1.0.0::CM026.document: CM026: Sneakers are not acceptable footwear at interviews, formal dinners, or weddings.

1.0.0::CM027.document: CM027: Flip flops are beach-only footwear.

1.0.0::CM028.document: CM028: Loafers are the most versatile smart-casual shoe.

1.0.0::CM029.document: CM029: Chelsea boots are the most versatile smart-casual boot.

1.0.0::CM030.document: CM030: Oxford shoes are the most formal shoe type.

1.0.0::CM031.document: CM031: Blazers can be dressed up with trousers and down with dark jeans.

1.0.0::CM032.document: CM032: A navy blazer is the single most versatile outer garment in menswear.

1.0.0::CM033.document: CM033: A blazer should never be mistaken for the jacket of a suit.

1.0.0::CM034.document: CM034: Polo shirts are not appropriate for formal business settings.

1.0.0::CM035.document: CM035: Oxford shirts are appropriate from casual to smart-casual only.

1.0.0::CM036.document: CM036: Dress shirts are appropriate from smart-casual to formal.

1.0.0::CM037.document: CM037: Graphic t-shirts are casual garments and should not be worn with tailoring.

1.0.0::CM038.document: CM038: Turtlenecks can replace a shirt and tie in semi-formal settings.

1.0.0::CM039.document: CM039: A white t-shirt under an open-collar dress shirt is always acceptable.

1.0.0::CM040.document: CM040: Roll shirt sleeves to the elbow to signal relaxed intent.

1.0.0::CM041.document: CM041: Knitwear adds texture without color complexity.

1.0.0::CM042.document: CM042: V-neck sweaters should always show a collar beneath them.

1.0.0::CM043.document: CM043: Cardigans layer over collared shirts for a smart-casual result.

1.0.0::CM044.document: CM044: Turtleneck + blazer is a timeless alternative to shirt + tie.

1.0.0::CM045.document: CM045: Trench coats elevate any outfit worn beneath them.

1.0.0::CM046.document: CM046: Bomber jackets belong in casual and smart-casual outfits only.

1.0.0::CM047.document: CM047: Parka is casual outerwear and should not be worn over formal attire.

1.0.0::CM048.document: CM048: Field jackets pair best with jeans, chinos, and casual trousers.

1.0.0::CM049.document: CM049: Overcoats are the most elegant form of outerwear.

1.0.0::CM050.document: CM050: Chinos are the bridge between jeans and formal trousers.

1.0.0::CM051.document: CM051: Cargo pants are casual garments — avoid with tailored or smart pieces.

1.0.0::CM052.document: CM052: Joggers and sweatpants belong in athleisure and gym contexts only.

1.0.0::CM053.document: CM053: Wide-leg trousers require a fitted top to balance silhouette.

1.0.0::CM054.document: CM054: Slim trousers pair with both fitted and slightly relaxed tops.

1.0.0::CM055.document: CM055: Shorts are casual and season-specific — avoid in autumn and winter.

1.0.0::CM056.document: CM056: Bermuda shorts are the most versatile short length for smart casual.

1.0.0::CM057.document: CM057: Linen is the ideal summer fabric — breathable and textured.

1.0.0::CM058.document: CM058: Wool is the most versatile cold-weather fabric.

1.0.0::CM059.document: CM059: Cashmere signals quality without effort.

1.0.0::CM060.document: CM060: Denim is an all-season fabric at the casual end of the spectrum.

1.0.0::CM061.document: CM061: Leather and suede belong in autumn and winter primarily.

1.0.0::CM062.document: CM062: Polyester and nylon are functional but signal lower quality in tailoring contexts.

1.0.0::CM063.document: CM063: Cotton is the most universal casual fabric.

1.0.0::CM064.document: CM064: Silk and satin are formal fabrics — avoid in casual settings.

1.0.0::CM065.document: CM065: Earth tones work year-round but peak in autumn.

1.0.0::CM066.document: CM066: Pastels are spring and summer colors.

1.0.0::CM067.document: CM067: Deep tones — burgundy, forest green, navy — are autumn and winter colors.

1.0.0::CM068.document: CM068: White and cream are summer and spring staples but can work year-round.

1.0.0::CM069.document: CM069: Black is appropriate year-round but is most natural in formal and winter contexts.

1.0.0::CM070.document: CM070: Mustard and olive are versatile earthy tones that pair with navy, brown, and gray.

1.0.0::CM071.document: CM071: Burgundy pairs with navy, gray, beige, and cream.

1.0.0::CM072.document: CM072: Teal pairs with navy, gray, white, and beige.

1.0.0::CM073.document: CM073: Red is an accent color — use sparingly.

1.0.0::CM074.document: CM074: Gold hardware and gold tones pair with warm colors; silver with cool.

1.0.0::CM075.document: CM075: Monochromatic outfits (same color family) look intentional and modern.

1.0.0::CM076.document: CM076: Tonal dressing requires different shades of the same hue — not the exact same tone.

1.0.0::CM077.document: CM077: One statement piece per outfit — let it breathe.

1.0.0::CM078.document: CM078: Clothes should fit your current body, not the body you plan to have.

1.0.0::CM079.document: CM079: Quality shoes and quality outerwear are the highest return investments in a wardrobe.

1.0.0::CM080.document: CM080: Occasion always dictates the formality ceiling of an outfit.

1.0.0::CM081.document: CM081: Smart casual is not an excuse to wear whatever you like — it has its own rules.

1.0.0::CM082.document: CM082: Business casual requires no denim, no graphic tees, no athletic wear.

1.0.0::CM083.document: CM083: Formal occasions require dark shoes, no exposed denim, and structured outerwear.

1.0.0::CM084.document: CM084: Beach and gym wear must not cross into any other occasion category.

1.0.0::CM085.document: CM085: Religious events require modest, clean, and occasion-appropriate clothing.

1.0.0::CM086.document: CM086: Heritage garments (oxford shirts, chinos, loafers) are always safe choices.

1.0.0::CM087.document: CM087: Simplicity always ages better than trend-driven complexity.

1.0.0::CM088.document: CM088: A well-maintained wardrobe of 20 pieces beats a cluttered wardrobe of 100.

1.0.0::CM089.document: CM089: Texture adds visual depth without introducing color risk.

1.0.0::CM090.document: CM090: Mixing textures within the same color family is always safe.

1.0.0::CM091.document: CM091: Pattern scale matters — a large check and a small stripe can coexist if separated by a solid.

1.0.0::CM092.document: CM092: The Ivy formula (oxford shirt + chinos + loafers) is the most reliable casual outfit in menswear.

1.0.0::CM093.document: CM093: The navy blazer formula (blazer + gray trousers + white shirt) is the most reliable smart-casual outfit.

1.0.0::CM094.document: CM094: The Americana formula (white tee + dark jeans + boots) is the most reliable casual outfit.

1.0.0::CM095.document: CM095: Dressing well is a learnable skill — it improves with observation and practice.

1.0.0::CM096.document: CM096: Study what works, not just what you like.

1.0.0::CM097.document: CM097: Personal style is built on mastered basics, not avant-garde experiments.

1.0.0::CM098.document: CM098: The best dressed men look effortless because they have internalized the rules.

1.0.0::CM099.document: CM099: Always consider the full silhouette, not individual garments.

1.0.0::CM100.document: CM100: The purpose of clothing is to serve the person wearing it — not the other way around.

1.0.0::CM101.document: CM101: Occasion, color, fit, and proportion — master these four and everything else follows.

1.0.0::CM102.document: CM102: When in doubt, wear navy, white, and well-fitted basics.

1.0.0::CM103.document: CM103: Your shoes are the first thing people notice and the last thing you should compromise on.

1.0.0::CM104.document: CM104: Clothes communicate context — wear what sends the right message for where you are going.

1.0.0::CM105.document: CM105: Ivy and prep style families share the same DNA: oxford cloth, chinos, loafers, and blazers.

1.0.0::CM106.document: CM106: Military-inspired garments (bombers, parkas, field jackets) belong in casual registers only.

1.0.0::CM107.document: CM107: Workwear and heritage garments earn credibility through age and patina — buy quality and wear it.

1.0.0::CM108.document: CM108: American style is democratic — it works for every body type when the fit is correct.

1.0.0::CM109.document: CM109: Never sacrifice comfort entirely for aesthetics — discomfort affects posture and confidence.

1.0.0::CM110.document: CM110: A great outfit starts with clean, well-maintained, properly stored garments.

1.0.0::SW001.document: SW001: The sneaker is chosen first in streetwear — the outfit is built around it.

1.0.0::SW002.document: SW002: Oversized tops must be balanced with slim or tapered bottoms.

1.0.0::SW003.document: SW003: Never wear an oversized top with an oversized bottom — silhouette collapses.

1.0.0::SW004.document: SW004: Pull at least one color from the sneaker and repeat it in the outfit.

1.0.0::SW005.document: SW005: All-white and all-black sneakers are neutrals — no color pull needed.

1.0.0::SW006.document: SW006: A graphic tee is the statement — all other pieces must be solid.

1.0.0::SW007.document: SW007: Never pair two graphic pieces in the same outfit.

1.0.0::SW008.document: SW008: One visible logo per outfit zone — no stacking logos in the same sightline.

1.0.0::SW009.document: SW009: Head-to-toe single-brand is an acceptable intentional statement.

1.0.0::SW010.document: SW010: Cargo pants work best with an oversized top, not a fitted one.

1.0.0::SW011.document: SW011: Cargo pants are casual — never wear them with tailored or luxury pieces.

1.0.0::SW012.document: SW012: Varsity jackets require a plain tee and simple trousers beneath.

1.0.0::SW013.document: SW013: Puffer jackets work best on a monochrome base — let the puffer be the only volume event.

1.0.0::SW014.document: SW014: A track jacket over a plain tee is the entry-level streetwear formula.

1.0.0::SW015.document: SW015: Color blocking in streetwear means two bold solids — one on top, one on bottom.

1.0.0::SW016.document: SW016: Never color-block with more than two saturated tones.

1.0.0::SW017.document: SW017: The streetwear neutral palette: black, white, gray, off-white, beige.

1.0.0::SW018.document: SW018: Earth tones (olive, tan, camel) work in streetwear as secondary neutrals.

1.0.0::SW019.document: SW019: Washed or faded tones signal vintage streetwear aesthetic.

1.0.0::SW020.document: SW020: Layering order: base tee → hoodie or flannel → outer jacket.

1.0.0::SW021.document: SW021: Each layer in streetwear layering should be slightly longer than the one beneath.

1.0.0::SW022.document: SW022: Open flannel over a tee creates effortless layering without bulk.

1.0.0::SW023.document: SW023: A boxy crewneck over a long tee (hem visible) is a deliberate layering gesture.

1.0.0::SW024.document: SW024: Shorts in streetwear hit above the knee — not basketball length, not micro.

1.0.0::SW025.document: SW025: Caps should match the dominant or accent color of the outfit.

1.0.0::SW026.document: SW026: Do not introduce a fourth color through a cap.

1.0.0::SW027.document: SW027: Beanies are a winter head accessory in streetwear — match outfit tone.

1.0.0::SW028.document: SW028: Crossbody bags in streetwear should be small and positioned at hip or chest.

1.0.0::SW029.document: SW029: Waist bags (fanny packs) are a techwear-adjacent streetwear accessory.

1.0.0::SW030.document: SW030: Chunky sneakers create bottom-heaviness — balance with a slim-fitting top.

1.0.0::SW031.document: SW031: Low-top sneakers are the most versatile streetwear footwear.

1.0.0::SW032.document: SW032: High-top sneakers visually raise the ankle — pair with shorter-length trousers.

1.0.0::SW033.document: SW033: Clean white sneakers are the most neutral streetwear footwear option.

1.0.0::SW034.document: SW034: The Air Force 1 is the most versatile streetwear sneaker — pairs with anything.

1.0.0::SW035.document: SW035: Timeless streetwear pieces: white tee, Levi's 501, Air Force 1, classic crewneck.

1.0.0::SW036.document: SW036: Hype pieces should accent an outfit, not anchor it.

1.0.0::SW037.document: SW037: A rare or loud statement piece requires a plain neutral backdrop.

1.0.0::SW038.document: SW038: Never wear two statement pieces in the same outfit.

1.0.0::SW039.document: SW039: Vintage or archive pieces should be treated as the focal item.

1.0.0::SW040.document: SW040: The hoodie is the most versatile streetwear top — works as both statement and base layer.

1.0.0::SW041.document: SW041: Zip hoodies function as light jackets — style them open over a tee.

1.0.0::SW042.document: SW042: Heavyweight cotton is the preferred streetwear fabric — it holds structure.

1.0.0::SW043.document: SW043: Washed fleece adds soft texture to streetwear outfits without formality.

1.0.0::SW044.document: SW044: Nylon windbreakers bridge streetwear and techwear.

1.0.0::SW045.document: SW045: Denim jackets in streetwear must be a different wash from denim bottoms.

1.0.0::SW046.document: SW046: Overshirts in streetwear can be worn fully open as a layer over tees.

1.0.0::SW047.document: SW047: Mesh or athletic shorts under a long tee — keep everything else minimal.

1.0.0::SW048.document: SW048: Sweatpants are streetwear-appropriate only in a fitted or tapered cut.

1.0.0::SW049.document: SW049: Wide-leg jeans in streetwear work best with a boxy or cropped top — not oversized.

1.0.0::SW050.document: SW050: The most reliable streetwear formula: white tee + dark jeans + clean sneaker.

1.0.0::SW051.document: SW051: The second most reliable formula: hoodie + cargo pants + chunky sneaker.

1.0.0::SW052.document: SW052: The third most reliable formula: varsity jacket + white tee + black jeans + Air Force 1.

1.0.0::SW053.document: SW053: Socks are visible in streetwear — match them to the color story or use white.

1.0.0::SW054.document: SW054: No-show socks with clean low-top sneakers is an acceptable minimal gesture.

1.0.0::SW055.document: SW055: Crew socks pulled high are a deliberate streetwear styling choice.

1.0.0::SW056.document: SW056: Do not mix athletic socks with luxury or minimal footwear.

1.0.0::SW057.document: SW057: Jewelry in streetwear: chain necklace, ring, or bracelet — one or two pieces maximum.

1.0.0::SW058.document: SW058: Sunglasses in streetwear should be bold in frame or tinted — not understated.

1.0.0::SW059.document: SW059: Camo print is a streetwear pattern — pair with a solid companion piece.

1.0.0::SW060.document: SW060: Tie-dye is a casual streetwear print — keep all other pieces plain.

1.0.0::SW061.document: SW061: Typography graphics read strongest against a plain, solid background.

1.0.0::SW062.document: SW062: All-over-print garments are the statement — wear with plain bottoms and sneakers only.

1.0.0::SW063.document: SW063: The bomber jacket is the most versatile streetwear outer piece after the hoodie.

1.0.0::SW064.document: SW064: MA-1 bombers pair with slim or straight trousers — not wide-leg.

1.0.0::SW065.document: SW065: Black on black in streetwear requires texture variation to avoid flat appearance.

1.0.0::SW066.document: SW066: White on white is a clean minimalist streetwear gesture — must have fit precision.

1.0.0::SW067.document: SW067: Gray is the most flexible streetwear base — it works with every accent color.

1.0.0::SW068.document: SW068: Never wear a graphic tee tucked in — it defeats the casual structure.

1.0.0::SW069.document: SW069: Streetwear silhouettes are never formal — avoid blazers and tailored trousers.

1.0.0::SW070.document: SW070: The coach jacket is an underrated versatile streetwear outer layer.

1.0.0::SW071.document: SW071: A heavy overshirt in flannel or canvas doubles as a streetwear jacket.

1.0.0::SW072.document: SW072: Fleece pullovers are a soft-casual streetwear piece — works with slim joggers.

1.0.0::SW073.document: SW073: Cargo shorts are acceptable in summer streetwear — keep them above the knee.

1.0.0::SW074.document: SW074: Technical pants (zippered vents, articulated knees) are techwear-influenced streetwear.

1.0.0::SW075.document: SW075: Never wear dress shoes with a streetwear outfit — the registers conflict.

1.0.0::SW076.document: SW076: Hiking boots can work in streetwear — gorpcore aesthetic.

1.0.0::SW077.document: SW077: Boots in streetwear (Timberland, combat) should be clean or deliberately distressed.

1.0.0::SW078.document: SW078: Streetwear does not have a formality ceiling — it is always casual.

1.0.0::SW079.document: SW079: The difference between streetwear and athleisure: streetwear uses fashion fabrics, athleisure uses performance fabrics.

1.0.0::SW080.document: SW080: Proportion is the skill — master volume balance and the rest follows.

1.0.0::SW081.document: SW081: Buy oversized intentionally — know your body's natural size and go one to two sizes up.

1.0.0::SW082.document: SW082: Oversized garments must still fit correctly in the shoulders.

1.0.0::SW083.document: SW083: Intentional distressing (faded, worn) reads authentically — factory distressing reads fake.

1.0.0::SW084.document: SW084: Minimal streetwear (plain tees, clean sneakers) is harder to execute than loud streetwear.

1.0.0::SW085.document: SW085: Streetwear rewards restraint — the most stylish outfits are often the simplest.

1.0.0::SW086.document: SW086: The graphic tee is the most personal garment in streetwear — it signals allegiance.

1.0.0::SW087.document: SW087: Band tees are streetwear heritage — wear them with respect for the reference.

1.0.0::SW088.document: SW088: Collaborations should be worn with the brand's visual language, not against it.

1.0.0::SW089.document: SW089: Season determines layering depth — not the number of pieces.

1.0.0::SW090.document: SW090: Streetwear is democratic — it does not require expensive pieces to execute well.

1.0.0::SW091.document: SW091: The quality of the basic pieces (tee, hoodie, chino) elevates the whole outfit.

1.0.0::SW092.document: SW092: Premium basics (heavyweight tee, sanforized denim) elevate streetwear to elevated casual.

1.0.0::SW093.document: SW093: Never iron or crease streetwear — it should look lived-in.

1.0.0::SW094.document: SW094: Sneaker cleanliness matters — a dirty sneaker undermines any outfit.

1.0.0::SW095.document: SW095: Sneaker colorways tell a story — know the story before you build around them.

1.0.0::SW096.document: SW096: New Balance 990 family reads as elevated casual streetwear — works with smart pieces.

1.0.0::SW097.document: SW097: Jordan 1 is the most versatile high-top for color-building outfits.

1.0.0::SW098.document: SW098: Air Force 1 Low in white is the universal neutral streetwear sneaker.

1.0.0::SW099.document: SW099: Chunky platform sneakers work best with slim, non-cuffed trousers.

1.0.0::SW100.document: SW100: Streetwear's greatest rule: wear it with confidence or it reads as a costume.

1.0.0::KF001.document: KF001: Wide trousers are the default bottom in Korean fashion — not an exception.

1.0.0::KF002.document: KF002: The top must be fitted, cropped, or minimally oversized when wearing wide trousers.

1.0.0::KF003.document: KF003: Double-wide silhouette (wide top + wide bottom) is only acceptable in intentional minimal compositions.

1.0.0::KF004.document: KF004: Tonal dressing means all colors share the same temperature — all warm or all cool.

1.0.0::KF005.document: KF005: Never mix warm and cool tones in Korean tonal outfits.

1.0.0::KF006.document: KF006: Muted, desaturated colors are the Korean palette — nothing fully saturated.

1.0.0::KF007.document: KF007: Dusty rose, sage green, slate blue, and stone gray are core Korean accent tones.

1.0.0::KF008.document: KF008: Beige, cream, ivory, and ecru are the primary Korean neutral tones.

1.0.0::KF009.document: KF009: Black and white are used as clean accents, not dominant forces.

1.0.0::KF010.document: KF010: Cropped tops paired with high-waist wide trousers is the defining Korean proportion.

1.0.0::KF011.document: KF011: A half-tuck of the shirt into wide trousers is the Korean smart-casual gesture.

1.0.0::KF012.document: KF012: The overshirt worn open is a core Korean casual layering piece.

1.0.0::KF013.document: KF013: Overshirts should be one size larger than your fitted size for the correct Korean drape.

1.0.0::KF014.document: KF014: Maximum two visible layers in a Korean outfit.

1.0.0::KF015.document: KF015: Layering in Korean fashion is always clean — no mismatched volumes.

1.0.0::KF016.document: KF016: Fine-gauge knitwear is preferred — chunky knits disrupt the minimal silhouette.

1.0.0::KF017.document: KF017: Boxy knits with straight-leg jeans is a reliable Korean autumn formula.

1.0.0::KF018.document: KF018: Mock-neck tops elevate plain outfits and are a core Korean wardrobe piece.

1.0.0::KF019.document: KF019: Turtlenecks in Korean fashion are fine-gauge and close-fitting at the neck.

1.0.0::KF020.document: KF020: Linen is the primary summer fabric — worn as shirts, trousers, or overshirts.

1.0.0::KF021.document: KF021: Cotton is the primary base fabric — plain and unbranded.

1.0.0::KF022.document: KF022: Silk is used sparingly in Korean fashion — as shirts or trouser fabric for elevated looks.

1.0.0::KF023.document: KF023: Technical fabrics do not belong in Korean fashion — this is techwear territory.

1.0.0::KF024.document: KF024: Clean white sneakers are the most versatile Korean fashion footwear.

1.0.0::KF025.document: KF025: Minimalist leather sneakers (Common Projects aesthetic) are the elevated Korean sneaker.

1.0.0::KF026.document: KF026: Suede loafers and penny loafers are smart-casual Korean footwear.

1.0.0::KF027.document: KF027: Clean derby or oxford shoes work in Korean fashion for smart-casual occasions.

1.0.0::KF028.document: KF028: Chunky sneakers are only acceptable in Korean streetwear — not minimal Korean fashion.

1.0.0::KF029.document: KF029: Sandals in Korean fashion are minimal leather — not sporty or technical.

1.0.0::KF030.document: KF030: No visible logos in Korean fashion — branding undermines the minimalism.

1.0.0::KF031.document: KF031: Accessories are minimal — one small bag, one subtle jewelry piece maximum.

1.0.0::KF032.document: KF032: A small structured tote or crossbody bag is the Korean fashion bag of choice.

1.0.0::KF033.document: KF033: Bucket hats are the most acceptable cap style in Korean fashion.

1.0.0::KF034.document: KF034: Baseball caps in Korean fashion are plain and unbranded.

1.0.0::KF035.document: KF035: Heavy accessory stacking belongs in Korean streetwear, not Korean minimal fashion.

1.0.0::KF036.document: KF036: The cropped jacket + wide trouser combination is the signature Korean fashion outfit.

1.0.0::KF037.document: KF037: Cropped jackets must be structured — soft or unstructured cropped jackets lose their balance.

1.0.0::KF038.document: KF038: Unstructured oversized coats are acceptable in Korean fashion as a single outer layer.

1.0.0::KF039.document: KF039: A minimal coat over a simple inner outfit is the Korean winter formula.

1.0.0::KF040.document: KF040: Pinstripe trousers are a subtle Korean smart-casual pattern — stay wide-leg.

1.0.0::KF041.document: KF041: Solid-color wide trousers are more versatile than patterned ones in Korean fashion.

1.0.0::KF042.document: KF042: Pleated wide trousers elevate a Korean outfit to smart-casual.

1.0.0::KF043.document: KF043: Flat-front wide trousers are the contemporary Korean casual option.

1.0.0::KF044.document: KF044: The hem of wide trousers should break cleanly at the ankle — no pooling, no cropped.

1.0.0::KF045.document: KF045: Straight-leg jeans are an acceptable alternative to wide trousers in casual Korean fashion.

1.0.0::KF046.document: KF046: Slim jeans are not part of the Korean fashion silhouette — too Western casual.

1.0.0::KF047.document: KF047: Overshirts in Korean fashion are linen, cotton, or lightweight technical fabrics.

1.0.0::KF048.document: KF048: Patterned overshirts should be subtle — micro-checks or tonal stripes only.

1.0.0::KF049.document: KF049: Bold-patterned tops require plain everything else in Korean fashion.

1.0.0::KF050.document: KF050: The full outfit should photograph as a single harmonious tone — this is the test.

1.0.0::KF051.document: KF051: Korean fashion is built for the editorial — every outfit should look intentional from 10 feet away.

1.0.0::KF052.document: KF052: Proportion is more important than brand in Korean fashion.

1.0.0::KF053.document: KF053: Fit precision matters — wide trousers must have the correct waist and length.

1.0.0::KF054.document: KF054: Seoul fashion uses the human body as architecture — clothing frames, not covers.

1.0.0::KF055.document: KF055: The Musinsa aesthetic: clean, minimal, proportional, tonal.

1.0.0::KF056.document: KF056: Seoul Fashion Week silhouettes filter into mainstream Korean casualwear within six months.

1.0.0::KF057.document: KF057: Oversized structured blazer + wide trousers is the elevated Korean smart-casual formula.

1.0.0::KF058.document: KF058: A knit vest over a plain tee is a distinctly Korean smart-casual layering move.

1.0.0::KF059.document: KF059: Knit vests should be fine-gauge and boxy, not fitted or chunky.

1.0.0::KF060.document: KF060: The Korean fashion color test: remove all labels and logos — the outfit should still read as cohesive.

1.0.0::KF061.document: KF061: High-waist trousers elevate any Korean casual outfit by one formality level.

1.0.0::KF062.document: KF062: Mid-rise wide trousers are more relaxed — appropriate for everyday casual.

1.0.0::KF063.document: KF063: Belts in Korean fashion are minimal and tonal — not a contrasting color.

1.0.0::KF064.document: KF064: No-belt with wide trousers relies on a well-fitted waist — this is the preference.

1.0.0::KF065.document: KF065: Summer Korean fashion: linen everything — shirt, trousers, overshirt in linen tones.

1.0.0::KF066.document: KF066: Winter Korean fashion: heavyweight knit, wide wool trousers, clean boots.

1.0.0::KF067.document: KF067: Korean fashion avoids sportswear references — this is not athleisure.

1.0.0::KF068.document: KF068: A simple, clean silhouette in muted tones always reads as Korean-influenced.

1.0.0::KF069.document: KF069: The half-tuck is reserved for casual contexts — full tuck for smart-casual.

1.0.0::KF070.document: KF070: Korean fashion is globally influential because it translates universally — neutrals and proportions work on any body.

1.0.0::KF071.document: KF071: Never rush the silhouette — wide trousers need the right length to land correctly.

1.0.0::KF072.document: KF072: Alterations are acceptable and encouraged — Korean fashion requires precision.

1.0.0::KF073.document: KF073: The Korean capsule wardrobe: wide trousers in 3 colors + 5 plain tops + 2 overshirts + clean sneakers.

1.0.0::KF074.document: KF074: Korean fashion is restrained — add one element at a time.

1.0.0::KF075.document: KF075: When in doubt in Korean fashion, remove one item from the outfit.

1.0.0::KF076.document: KF076: A plain white tee is the most useful Korean fashion top — universal base layer.

1.0.0::KF077.document: KF077: Striped tees in Korean fashion are horizontal, fine-gauge, and worn with plain wide trousers.

1.0.0::KF078.document: KF078: Korean fashion is quiet confidence — it does not demand attention.

1.0.0::KF079.document: KF079: The texture of the fabric communicates quality in Korean fashion — touch test.

1.0.0::KF080.document: KF080: Buying one excellent wide trouser is more valuable than five mediocre ones in Korean fashion.

1.0.0::KF081.document: KF081: Garment care matters — wrinkles in Korean fashion read as carelessness.

1.0.0::KF082.document: KF082: Linen wrinkles are acceptable — they are part of the fabric's character.

1.0.0::KF083.document: KF083: Steaming is the Korean fashion garment care tool of choice.

1.0.0::KF084.document: KF084: Color palette discipline is the hardest Korean fashion skill to master.

1.0.0::KF085.document: KF085: The warm palette: stone, ecru, camel, sand, tan, dusty orange.

1.0.0::KF086.document: KF086: The cool palette: slate, ash gray, navy, powder blue, off-white.

1.0.0::KF087.document: KF087: Mixing a warm and cool tone by accident is the most common Korean fashion mistake.

1.0.0::KF088.document: KF088: Natural light is the test for tone temperature — check your outfit in daylight.

1.0.0::KF089.document: KF089: Korean fashion evolves faster than Western minimalism — stay close to Musinsa and Seoul Fashion Week references.

1.0.0::KF090.document: KF090: Korean smart casual does not require a jacket — proportional tops and wide trousers are enough.

1.0.0::KF091.document: KF091: A minimal structured bag completes a Korean outfit the way a blazer completes a Western one.

1.0.0::KF092.document: KF092: Footwear is the final decision in Korean fashion — it must land cleanly under the wide trouser hem.

1.0.0::KF093.document: KF093: Clean rubber or gum sole is preferable to technical or chunky sole in Korean fashion.

1.0.0::KF094.document: KF094: Footwear color should be white, cream, tan, or a tone already present in the outfit.

1.0.0::KF095.document: KF095: Do not introduce a new color through footwear in Korean fashion.

1.0.0::KF096.document: KF096: Korean fashion achieves personality through proportion, not decoration.

1.0.0::KF097.document: KF097: The silhouette tells the story — everything else is supporting cast.

1.0.0::KF098.document: KF098: Negative space in the silhouette (the wide trouser drape, the overshirt opening) is intentional.

1.0.0::KF099.document: KF099: Korean fashion is not minimalism for its own sake — it is precision in service of effortlessness.

1.0.0::KF100.document: KF100: Master the wide trouser silhouette first — everything else in Korean fashion flows from it.

1.0.0::TW001.document: TW001: Base layer manages moisture, mid layer manages temperature, shell layer manages weather.

1.0.0::TW002.document: TW002: Never skip the base layer — moisture accumulation destroys the comfort of outer layers.

1.0.0::TW003.document: TW003: Every garment in a techwear outfit must have a functional justification.

1.0.0::TW004.document: TW004: GORE-TEX is the benchmark weatherproofing fabric — all alternatives are compromises.

1.0.0::TW005.document: TW005: Sealed seams are non-negotiable in a true waterproof system.

1.0.0::TW006.document: TW006: DWR (Durable Water Repellent) treatment is the minimum weatherproofing for a techwear shell.

1.0.0::TW007.document: TW007: Nylon ripstop is the most versatile techwear fabric — lightweight, abrasion-resistant, packable.

1.0.0::TW008.document: TW008: Schoeller stretch fabric allows articulated movement in structured techwear pants.

1.0.0::TW009.document: TW009: Technical fabrics should not be mixed with raw denim or heavy cotton in the same outfit.

1.0.0::TW010.document: TW010: All-black is the foundational techwear palette.

1.0.0::TW011.document: TW011: Black + olive is the second most reliable techwear palette.

1.0.0::TW012.document: TW012: Black + stone or gray is the third most reliable techwear palette.

1.0.0::TW013.document: TW013: Bright colors have no place in serious techwear.

1.0.0::TW014.document: TW014: Hi-vis or safety orange is the only acceptable bright accent in techwear — functional, not decorative.

1.0.0::TW015.document: TW015: Coyote brown and ranger green are acceptable techwear earth tone alternatives to all-black.

1.0.0::TW016.document: TW016: Techwear silhouettes are articulated — pre-shaped at the elbow and knee for movement.

1.0.0::TW017.document: TW017: Tapered or adjustable ankle openings are the standard for techwear pants.

1.0.0::TW018.document: TW018: Wide-leg cuts are not techwear — they conflict with the articulated, functional silhouette.

1.0.0::TW019.document: TW019: Every zipper, buckle, and strap must have a functional purpose.

1.0.0::TW020.document: TW020: Decorative hardware that mimics techwear without function is a costume, not techwear.

1.0.0::TW021.document: TW021: Pockets must be accessible with one hand and positioned for movement.

1.0.0::TW022.document: TW022: Chest pockets reduce the need for a separate bag — optimize pocket placement.

1.0.0::TW023.document: TW023: Thigh pockets on cargo pants must not restrict stride — position and size matter.

1.0.0::TW024.document: TW024: Velcro closures are acceptable in techwear — they provide quick access.

1.0.0::TW025.document: TW025: Magnetic closures are the premium techwear fastener — Acronym uses them extensively.

1.0.0::TW026.document: TW026: Trail runners are the primary techwear footwear — lug sole, waterproof, technical.

1.0.0::TW027.document: TW027: Salomon XT-6 and XT-Wings are the reference trail runners for techwear.

1.0.0::TW028.document: TW028: Nike ACG footwear bridges techwear and streetwear aesthetics.

1.0.0::TW029.document: TW029: Technical boots (waterproof, lug sole) are for wet or heavy terrain techwear outfits.

1.0.0::TW030.document: TW030: Leather shoes do not belong in techwear — the material conflicts with the philosophy.

1.0.0::TW031.document: TW031: Chest rigs are acceptable modular accessories in techwear — one per outfit.

1.0.0::TW032.document: TW032: Waist bags and hip packs provide hands-free storage in techwear — keep them small.

1.0.0::TW033.document: TW033: Modular bag attachment (MOLLE, D-ring) keeps the silhouette clean and organized.

1.0.0::TW034.document: TW034: Technical backpacks in techwear should be technical fabrics — no canvas or leather.

1.0.0::TW035.document: TW035: One storage solution per outfit — do not stack waist bag + chest rig + backpack.

1.0.0::TW036.document: TW036: Acronym is the reference brand for functional modular techwear.

1.0.0::TW037.document: TW037: Veilance is the reference brand for refined urban techwear.

1.0.0::TW038.document: TW038: Nike ACG is the accessible entry point for techwear aesthetics.

1.0.0::TW039.document: TW039: Arc'teryx bridges outdoor performance and urban techwear most successfully.

1.0.0::TW040.document: TW040: Budget techwear should prioritize function over aesthetics — a cheap GORE-TEX shell beats an expensive non-waterproof one.

1.0.0::TW041.document: TW041: Layering in techwear is weather-driven — add or remove layers based on conditions, not looks.

1.0.0::TW042.document: TW042: A shell alone in warm, mild weather is a complete techwear outfit.

1.0.0::TW043.document: TW043: A shell + mid + base is the complete three-layer cold-weather techwear system.

1.0.0::TW044.document: TW044: Insulated jackets as outer layers (without a shell) are acceptable in dry cold weather.

1.0.0::TW045.document: TW045: Never wear a fleece as an outer layer in rain — it absorbs water.

1.0.0::TW046.document: TW046: Down insulation compresses well but loses insulation when wet — use synthetic in wet conditions.

1.0.0::TW047.document: TW047: Merino wool base layers regulate temperature better than polyester in extreme cold.

1.0.0::TW048.document: TW048: Ultralight packing capacity is a techwear feature — packable jackets provide versatility.

1.0.0::TW049.document: TW049: Hood design matters — a helmet-compatible hood is the techwear standard.

1.0.0::TW050.document: TW050: Pit zips and underarm venting regulate temperature during activity in techwear.

1.0.0::TW051.document: TW051: Techwear is performance first — if the outfit restricts movement, it fails.

1.0.0::TW052.document: TW052: Test a techwear outfit by crouching, reaching overhead, and twisting — it should accommodate all.

1.0.0::TW053.document: TW053: Articulated elbows mean the sleeve maintains its bend without pulling.

1.0.0::TW054.document: TW054: Gusseted crotch on technical pants allows squat and step without restriction.

1.0.0::TW055.document: TW055: Adjustable cuffs (velcro, snapback) seal the wrist gap between glove and sleeve.

1.0.0::TW056.document: TW056: Packable pouches that convert into the jacket's chest pocket are a Veilance-style feature.

1.0.0::TW057.document: TW057: Reflective details in techwear are safety features — they also add visual depth at night.

1.0.0::TW058.document: TW058: Laser perforations in technical fabrics provide breathability without sacrificing weather resistance.

1.0.0::TW059.document: TW059: 3-layer GORE-TEX construction is more durable than 2.5-layer — the face fabric has a separate backer.

1.0.0::TW060.document: TW060: Waterproof zippers (YKK Aquaguard) are the techwear zipper standard.

1.0.0::TW061.document: TW061: Techwear does not need to be expensive — function is the measure, not brand.

1.0.0::TW062.document: TW062: A $200 technical rain shell outperforms a $2000 fashion piece that is not weatherproof.

1.0.0::TW063.document: TW063: Urban techwear (Veilance, Acronym) bridges function and refined aesthetics.

1.0.0::TW064.document: TW064: Outdoor techwear (Arc'teryx Alpha, Patagonia Torrentshell) is function-first.

1.0.0::TW065.document: TW065: The difference between techwear and gorpcore: techwear is urban and architectural, gorpcore is outdoor and casual.

1.0.0::TW066.document: TW066: Gorpcore uses techwear pieces in casual, non-tactical contexts — it is a streetwear adjacent style.

1.0.0::TW067.document: TW067: Black technical pants are more versatile than olive in urban techwear contexts.

1.0.0::TW068.document: TW068: Olive technical pants are more versatile in outdoor or mixed urban-outdoor techwear.

1.0.0::TW069.document: TW069: Stone and gray technical pants bridge indoor and outdoor techwear contexts.

1.0.0::TW070.document: TW070: Never wear techwear to a formal occasion — the fabrics and silhouettes do not translate.

1.0.0::TW071.document: TW071: Techwear is never warm-weather casual — it is always purposeful dressing.

1.0.0::TW072.document: TW072: Summer techwear: ultralight shell + technical shorts + trail runners (minimal three-layer system).

1.0.0::TW073.document: TW073: Technical shorts in techwear: nylon, quick-dry, above-knee.

1.0.0::TW074.document: TW074: Technical T-shirts (merino, performance mesh) are acceptable summer techwear base layers.

1.0.0::TW075.document: TW075: Full techwear in summer is impractical and defeats the functional logic.

1.0.0::TW076.document: TW076: Always check the weather rating of a technical fabric before purchasing.

1.0.0::TW077.document: TW077: Waterproof rating: 10,000mm hydrostatic head is the minimum for reliable rain protection.

1.0.0::TW078.document: TW078: Breathability rating: 10,000 g/m² moisture vapor transmission rate minimum.

1.0.0::TW079.document: TW079: A non-breathable waterproof shell creates internal condensation — unacceptable in serious techwear.

1.0.0::TW080.document: TW080: Care instructions for technical fabrics: wash without fabric softener — it blocks DWR pores.

1.0.0::TW081.document: TW081: Reactivate DWR treatment by tumble-drying on low after washing.

1.0.0::TW082.document: TW082: Technical fabrics degrade with improper care — follow garment instructions precisely.

1.0.0::TW083.document: TW083: Techwear is an investment — maintain it properly for multi-year use.

1.0.0::TW084.document: TW084: Acronym and Veilance pieces retain value because of their functional construction quality.

1.0.0::TW085.document: TW085: The techwear silhouette reads as architectural — structure, shadow, and modularity.

1.0.0::TW086.document: TW086: Photography reveals techwear quality — technical fabrics have distinctive light behavior.

1.0.0::TW087.document: TW087: A complete techwear outfit should be identifiable as techwear from 20 meters.

1.0.0::TW088.document: TW088: Never substitute non-technical pieces in a techwear outfit just for aesthetics.

1.0.0::TW089.document: TW089: The Acronym design philosophy: every detail serves multiple functions simultaneously.

1.0.0::TW090.document: TW090: A good techwear shell should last 5+ years with proper care.

1.0.0::TW091.document: TW091: Technical footwear maintenance: clean with a soft brush, re-waterproof with spray treatment.

1.0.0::TW092.document: TW092: A techwear outfit's quality is tested by the weather it is worn in.

1.0.0::TW093.document: TW093: Urban techwear works in all conditions — the city is the terrain.

1.0.0::TW094.document: TW094: Modular systems allow one outfit to adapt to morning warmth and evening cold.

1.0.0::TW095.document: TW095: The helmet-compatible hood, when worn down, creates a specific techwear drape — intentional.

1.0.0::TW096.document: TW096: Techwear is a commitment — you cannot half-execute it with one technical piece and everything else casual.

1.0.0::TW097.document: TW097: Entry point techwear: Nike ACG windrunner + Nike ACG cargo pants + trail runners.

1.0.0::TW098.document: TW098: Advanced techwear: Acronym J1A-GT + Acronym P10-DS + Salomon XT-6.

1.0.0::TW099.document: TW099: Techwear mastery is achieved when function and aesthetics are completely unified.

1.0.0::TW100.document: TW100: The ultimate techwear test: wear it in a storm and judge it on what it does, not how it looks.

1.0.0::LX001.document: LX001: Quiet luxury communicates through fabric quality and restraint — not logos.

1.0.0::LX002.document: LX002: The luxury test: remove all labels — if the garment still communicates quality, it passes.

1.0.0::LX003.document: LX003: Cashmere is the foundational luxury fabric — invest in it before any other.

1.0.0::LX004.document: LX004: Vicuña is the most luxurious natural fiber — reserved for the highest tier.

1.0.0::LX005.document: LX005: Fine merino wool is the everyday luxury fabric — versatile across seasons.

1.0.0::LX006.document: LX006: Silk communicates luxury through its light behavior — it moves differently than any other fabric.

1.0.0::LX007.document: LX007: Suede communicates luxury through tactile richness — it elevates any outfit it touches.

1.0.0::LX008.document: LX008: Double-face wool is the luxury outerwear fabric standard — clean on both sides, substantial.

1.0.0::LX009.document: LX009: Linen is the summer luxury fabric — it wrinkles intentionally and breathes perfectly.

1.0.0::LX010.document: LX010: Avoid polyester, nylon, and acrylic in any luxury context — they signal economy.

1.0.0::LX011.document: LX011: Neutral palette is the luxury standard — stone, ecru, ivory, sand, slate, navy, charcoal.

1.0.0::LX012.document: LX012: Never more than two colors in a luxury outfit.

1.0.0::LX013.document: LX013: When wearing three tones, all three must be neutrals.

1.0.0::LX014.document: LX014: Accent colors in luxury are introduced seasonally: burgundy in winter, pale blue in summer.

1.0.0::LX015.document: LX015: Texture replaces color as the primary visual interest in luxury dressing.

1.0.0::LX016.document: LX016: Texture hierarchy: finer textures toward the body, coarser outward.

1.0.0::LX017.document: LX017: Never layer two high-sheen fabrics — silk + satin creates visual competition.

1.0.0::LX018.document: LX018: Mixing a matte fabric with a subtle sheen fabric creates refined contrast.

1.0.0::LX019.document: LX019: Bouclé or textured wool jacket over a smooth merino turtleneck is the texture principle in practice.

1.0.0::LX020.document: LX020: Sprezzatura — the appearance of effortlessness — is the goal of all luxury dressing.

1.0.0::LX021.document: LX021: An outfit that looks too coordinated has lost its sprezzatura.

1.0.0::LX022.document: LX022: Roll the trouser cuff once, casually, to signal sprezzatura.

1.0.0::LX023.document: LX023: Leave the bottom button of a jacket perpetually undone — this is not carelessness, it is tradition.

1.0.0::LX024.document: LX024: Drape a cashmere sweater over the shoulders — the Italian gesture of relaxed luxury.

1.0.0::LX025.document: LX025: Slight rumpling of a linen shirt is acceptable and authentic — do not over-press linen.

1.0.0::LX026.document: LX026: Unstructured blazers communicate modern luxury — remove the padding, preserve the craft.

1.0.0::LX027.document: LX027: A soft-shoulder blazer should feel like a cardigan in weight — but look like a jacket.

1.0.0::LX028.document: LX028: The Brunello Cucinelli standard: clothes that look simple, feel extraordinary, and cost accordingly.

1.0.0::LX029.document: LX029: The Loro Piana standard: technical fabric mastery applied to luxury casualwear.

1.0.0::LX030.document: LX030: Tom Ford standard: precise tailoring, dark palette, controlled sensuality.

1.0.0::LX031.document: LX031: Suede loafers are the most versatile luxury casual shoe.

1.0.0::LX032.document: LX032: Penny loafers in leather or suede are the second most versatile luxury casual shoe.

1.0.0::LX033.document: LX033: Hand-welted shoes (Goodyear or Norwegian welt) signal construction quality in luxury footwear.

1.0.0::LX034.document: LX034: Patent leather is strictly formal — do not wear it in casual or smart-casual luxury contexts.

1.0.0::LX035.document: LX035: Chelsea boots in suede or fine leather are the luxury boot of choice.

1.0.0::LX036.document: LX036: Never wear athletic sneakers with luxury clothing — the material registers conflict.

1.0.0::LX037.document: LX037: Luxury sneakers (Common Projects, Maison Margiela Tabi) are the only sneaker exception.

1.0.0::LX038.document: LX038: Belt color must match shoe color in luxury contexts — always.

1.0.0::LX039.document: LX039: A visible belt in luxury dressing should be thin, leather, and in the same tone as shoes.

1.0.0::LX040.document: LX040: No belt with pleated trousers is the Italian preference — use braces instead.

1.0.0::LX041.document: LX041: Braces (suspenders) in luxury dressing are under the jacket — not visible.

1.0.0::LX042.document: LX042: Pocket squares are a luxury accessory — linen in white or cream for formal; silk for semi-formal.

1.0.0::LX043.document: LX043: The pocket square should complement, never perfectly match, the tie.

1.0.0::LX044.document: LX044: A watch is the only jewelry that is fully acceptable in all luxury contexts.

1.0.0::LX045.document: LX045: A watch in luxury dressing is a mechanical timepiece — not a smartwatch.

1.0.0::LX046.document: LX046: Fine knitwear is the bridge between casualwear and luxury tailoring.

1.0.0::LX047.document: LX047: A cashmere crewneck over an oxford cloth shirt = the most reliable luxury casual combination.

1.0.0::LX048.document: LX048: A turtleneck under a soft blazer replaces shirt and tie in luxury smart-casual contexts.

1.0.0::LX049.document: LX049: The relaxed luxury formula: fine knit + tailored trousers + suede loafers.

1.0.0::LX050.document: LX050: The summer luxury formula: linen shirt + silk or linen wide trousers + leather sandals.

1.0.0::LX051.document: LX051: The winter luxury formula: cashmere rollneck + double-face wool coat + flannel trousers + suede boots.

1.0.0::LX052.document: LX052: Layering in luxury is always fine — a silk scarf under a wool coat adds warmth without bulk.

1.0.0::LX053.document: LX053: Never layer bulky items in luxury — each layer must be fine-gauge or fine-woven.

1.0.0::LX054.document: LX054: The overcoat is the luxury outer garment — it communicates status before you enter a room.

1.0.0::LX055.document: LX055: A double-breasted overcoat in charcoal or camel is the most powerful luxury coat silhouette.

1.0.0::LX056.document: LX056: Invest in one extraordinary coat before expanding the wardrobe further.

1.0.0::LX057.document: LX057: Trousers in luxury dressing should have a light break or no break — full breaks are dated.

1.0.0::LX058.document: LX058: Wide trousers in fine wool or silk are acceptable luxury bottoms — they reference Italian ease.

1.0.0::LX059.document: LX059: Pleated trousers in luxury dressing allow movement without compromising the silhouette.

1.0.0::LX060.document: LX060: Flat-front slim trousers are the contemporary luxury standard — structured and clean.

1.0.0::LX061.document: LX061: Shorts are only acceptable in luxury casual in linen, at resort or holiday settings.

1.0.0::LX062.document: LX062: No athletic shorts, sweatpants, or joggers belong in luxury contexts.

1.0.0::LX063.document: LX063: Denim is acceptable in luxury casual if it is dark, slim, and unembellished.

1.0.0::LX064.document: LX064: Raw or dry denim is more aligned with luxury than pre-washed or distressed.

1.0.0::LX065.document: LX065: Luxury casual is the hardest register to master — nothing to hide behind.

1.0.0::LX066.document: LX066: Quality is communicated subliminally — people feel the quality before they identify it.

1.0.0::LX067.document: LX067: Buy fewer, better garments — ten luxury pieces outperform fifty mediocre ones.

1.0.0::LX068.document: LX068: Invest in the categories with the highest visible impact: coat, shoe, and knitwear.

1.0.0::LX069.document: LX069: A luxury garment should last 10+ years with proper care.

1.0.0::LX070.document: LX070: Dry-cleaning cashmere too often destroys the fiber — hand-wash with gentle detergent.

1.0.0::LX071.document: LX071: Store cashmere folded, never on a hanger — it stretches under its own weight.

1.0.0::LX072.document: LX072: Suede requires a suede brush and water repellent spray — treat before first wear.

1.0.0::LX073.document: LX073: Leather shoes should be cedar-shoe-treed after every wear to maintain shape.

1.0.0::LX074.document: LX074: Rotate footwear — never wear the same pair two days in a row.

1.0.0::LX075.document: LX075: Well-maintained luxury garments develop patina — a quality that cannot be bought, only earned.

1.0.0::LX076.document: LX076: Tailoring is the final luxury investment — even excellent garments benefit from it.

1.0.0::LX077.document: LX077: Hemming, tapering, and taking in the chest are the three most valuable luxury alterations.

1.0.0::LX078.document: LX078: The shoulder fit of a luxury jacket cannot be tailored easily — buy for the shoulder first.

1.0.0::LX079.document: LX079: A suit from an Italian or British maker in a classic cut needs no trend validation.

1.0.0::LX080.document: LX080: Classic colors in tailoring (navy, charcoal, mid-gray) remain relevant indefinitely.

1.0.0::LX081.document: LX081: Avoid fashion trends in luxury investment pieces — they date garments.

1.0.0::LX082.document: LX082: Bold lapels, extreme cuts, and statement patterns are trend items — not luxury investments.

1.0.0::LX083.document: LX083: The minimal, clean luxury look has an indefinite shelf life.

1.0.0::LX084.document: LX084: Italian luxury style is founded on fabric, fit, and color restraint — in that order.

1.0.0::LX085.document: LX085: British luxury style adds heritage and construction rigor — Savile Row standard.

1.0.0::LX086.document: LX086: French luxury style is the most architectural — structured and controlled.

1.0.0::LX087.document: LX087: The combination of Italian ease, British construction, and French restraint is the highest luxury standard.

1.0.0::LX088.document: LX088: Luxury dressing is not about spending the most — it is about spending correctly.

1.0.0::LX089.document: LX089: A Neapolitan handmade suit is a lifetime investment — it improves with age.

1.0.0::LX090.document: LX090: The luxury wardrobe is a curation — every piece must justify its presence.

1.0.0::LX091.document: LX091: Navy blazer + gray flannel trousers + white shirt = the irreducible luxury smart-casual formula.

1.0.0::LX092.document: LX092: Cashmere sport coat + merino turtleneck + tailored trousers = the modern Italian luxury formula.

1.0.0::LX093.document: LX093: Linen suit in stone or ivory = the summer luxury formula.

1.0.0::LX094.document: LX094: Double-face wool overcoat + fine knit + flannel trousers = the winter luxury formula.

1.0.0::LX095.document: LX095: The luxury man owns less than the average man — but every piece is extraordinary.

1.0.0::LX096.document: LX096: Confidence is the final luxury garment — it cannot be purchased.

1.0.0::LX097.document: LX097: Luxury dressing is not performance — it is a private relationship with quality.

1.0.0::LX098.document: LX098: The best-dressed luxury men are invisible — their clothes do not draw attention, they command respect.

1.0.0::LX099.document: LX099: True luxury is dressing for yourself — not for others to recognize the brand.

1.0.0::LX100.document: LX100: When every decision is right — fabric, fit, color, proportion — the result is effortless elegance.
